thread:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — we just got an enterprise escalation from AcmeCorp. They report a surge of 401s starting ~08:12 UTC across multiple regions. Error messages vary between 'invalid signature' and 'token expired'.

Alex Chen: ack. any request IDs or sample tokens in the ticket?

Maya Patel: ticket includes a sample token (redacted) and logs. Example from proxy logs: `auth.verify: JWT validation failed: signature verification failed` and also `auth.verify: token expired (exp < now)` for different requests. Sending snippets.

Maya Patel: repro notes from support: they get success with the same client creds when calling our hosted-api in us-west-2 but fail in eu-central-1. They said tokens are minted by their IdP (Okta) with kid missing sometimes.

Jen Rivera: hmm — two separate classes of errors. Could be: (A) clock skew causing valid tokens to be considered expired, (B) signature algorithm / kid mismatch causing invalid signature. We should check JWKS caching/refresh behavior + alg/kid handling in the verifier.

Luis Gomez: I pulled verifier logs around 08:12. We see a bunch of 200 responses from the jwks endpoint but with different payloads (same issuer, different key sets). Infra seems to be fronting jwks via our jwks-proxy which had a rolling deploy at 08:09. Could be a race where cache returned old keys while tokens were minted against a new key.

Alex Chen: can you paste the exact verifier error stack?

Maya Patel: here you go (sanitized):
```
verify_jwt.go:142: VerifyToken failed: signature verification failed
jwt/validator.go:87: error validating token: key not found for kid ""
httpproxy/jwks_cache.go:56: cache miss; fetching JWKS from https://idp.acme/.well-known/jwks.json
httpproxy/jwks_cache.go:82: fetched JWKS (etag="W/\"12345\"") status=200
```

Alex Chen: note `kid ""` — the token had no kid header. If the jwks contains multiple keys we need to attempt matching by alg+use or fallback to trying all possible keys. Our verifier currently requires kid when >1 key in set. That explains "key not found" -> signature error.

Jen Rivera: also, the 'token expired' events — did you check clocks?

Luis Gomez: yes — one of our eu-central nodes had NTP drift of ~90s at 08:10 due to a transient chronyd issue during the jwks-proxy deploy. So some nodes validated exp/nbf incorrectly.

Maya Patel: customer timeline matches: tokens minted at 08:11, some requests routed to drifted node -> expired. Others routed to node that attempted verification without kid -> brute-forced keys -> signature failed (we treat that as fatal).

Alex Chen: repro steps I used locally:
1) curl to IdP JWKS and save file
2) create a token signed with a rotated key (ES256) and a header without kid:
```
header={"alg":"ES256","typ":"JWT"}
payload={"iss":"https://idp.acme","sub":"u123","exp":$(date -d '+5 minutes' +%s)}
# signature with private key -> token
```
3) run our verifier binary pointing at saved jwks -> fails with "key not found" because jwks has keys with kid values, alg RS256 and ES256 mixed

Alex Chen: additionally I tried reproducing clock skew: `date -s '+2 minutes'` and validation started returning expired for tokens minted just now.

Jen Rivera: ok action plan: short term fix (hotpatch) and medium-term robustness.

Juan (deploy-bot): Rolling deploy of jwks-proxy v2.3.1 started at 08:09 UTC (by infra).

Luis Gomez: short-term hotpatch suggestions: 1) relax allowed clock skew tolerance in verifier from 30s -> 120s for edge regions, 2) when kid missing, try fallback: iterate all keys in JWKS with matching alg+use and attempt verification instead of immediate reject, 3) invalidate JWKS cache on deploy events / 5xx/dirty ETag.

Jen Rivera: agree but be careful: brute-forcing keys increases CPU cost; limit it to when kid is absent AND jwks size <= 5. Also add metrics/logging to track how often fallback happens.

Maya Patel: Support asked for a clear repro they can run. Can we craft a curl+jq reproducible snippet they can run that mimics the broken path?

Alex Chen: yes — put this in the ticket (sanitized):
```
# fetch jwks
curl -sS "https://idp.acme/.well-known/jwks.json" -o /tmp/jwks.json
# craft header without kid
hdr='{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT"}'
payld='{"iss":"https://idp.acme","sub":"test","exp":'$(( $(date +%s)+120 ))'}'
# sign locally with a different key (private key in PEM)
header_b64=$(echo -n "$hdr" | openssl base64 -e | tr -d '=\n' | tr '/+' '_-' )
payload_b64=$(echo -n "$payld" | openssl base64 -e | tr -d '=\n' | tr '/+' '_-' )
sig=$(printf "%s.%s" "$header_b64" "$payload_b64" | openssl dgst -sha256 -sign ./other_key.pem | openssl base64 -e | tr -d '=\n' | tr '/+' '_-')
token="$header_b64.$payload_b64.$sig"
# call our API
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" https://api.redwood.example/v1/using-endpoint
```
Note: adjust alg/signing to match mismatch scenario (ES256 vs RS256)

Maya Patel: good. What's the rollout plan for the hotpatch?

Luis Gomez: propose: patch verifier lib (go/jwtlib) to add fallback-try-all-when-kid-missing + increase skew to 120s behind a feature flag. Canary in eu-central-1 only (10% traffic) for 30m, monitor auth failures, latencies, CPU. If green, flip global.

Jen Rivera: also add cache invalidation hook in jwks-proxy: whenever it observes a 5xx from origin or ETag change -> immediately purge local caches and revalidate. Plus expose a /admin/clear-cache endpoint (auth only) so we can clear per-tenant on support request.

support-bot: Ticket #45321 updated: sent repro + workaround to AcmeCorp, requested poisson rollout.

Maya Patel: I'll own customer comms. Keep me posted on canary. Luis/Jen/Alex will you triage and push the patch?

Luis Gomez: on it. Starting branch now: git checkout -b fix/jwks-fallback-skew

Alex Chen: I'll prepare unit tests (missing-kid, multiple-keys, clock-skew windows) and a small benchmark for fallback to ensure we don't spike CPU.

Jen Rivera: I'll coordinate deploy and canary config. Also will schedule a short postmortem once resolved.

Maya Patel: thanks all. Please paste the deployment PR when ready and tag me so I can update the support ticket. :thumbsup:

Alex Chen: PR 4382 created: add kid-less fallback, skew flag, cache invalidation hook. Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/verify-service/pulls/4382

Luis Gomez: canary is up in eu-central-1 10% traffic at 09:05 UTC. Monitoring auth.failures metric now.

infra-bot: Canary health check: 09:10 UTC: auth.failures (p95) dropped from 2.3% -> 0.4% in canary group. CPU usage +4% on verifier pods.

Maya Patel: great initial signal. I'll close the loop with AcmeCorp and propose permanent config changes (skew tolerance + admin cache clear). We'll follow up in the postmortem with timeline + root causes (deploy + NTP drift + kid-less tokens + mismatch alg).

Jen Rivera: adding TODOs: (1) audit other verifiers for same codepath, (2) add instrumentation for kid-missing fallbacks, (3) ensure jwks-proxy deploys don't cause stale caches during rollout.

Maya Patel: thanks team. I'll drop a short incident summary into #postmortems after we gather metrics.
